summary: Saturn's 19-year mahadasha is described in the general texts as a slow, burdensome period: illness in the family, losses in farming and property, absence from home, servants leaving and sudden losses. Every classical source makes it strongly conditional: in its own, exalted or friendly sign, in the 3rd or 11th, in a kendra or trikona, in Sagittarius or Pisces, with benefics or as a yogakaraka it gives high position, property, wealth and children; in the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated or combust it brings danger, imprisonment, separation from parents and trouble to spouse and children.
common_outcomes: wind ailments such as gout or rheumatism in the family, losses in farming, gossip and slander, servants leaving, long stays away from home, sudden losses of relatives, land, comfort and wealth (Phaladeepika 19.13)

gains of servants, elderly women and cattle, sometimes through unrest in the country, alongside trouble to spouse and children, wind and phlegm disorders, piles and burning in the limbs (Phaladeepika 19.23)
possession of livestock and coarse grain, earnings from running a guild, trade body or village community (Jataka Parijata 18.121)
when well placed: recognition from government, wealth, conveyances, a high post such as command of an army, gain of property and birth of children (BPHS 47.53-56)
when badly placed: danger from poison and weapons, separation from father, distress to wife and children, trouble from government displeasure, imprisonment (BPHS 47.57-58)
rare_outcomes: rule over a low tribe or a village, or headship of a village or small town (Jataka Parijata 18.121; Uttara Kalamrita sec. 6, sl. 11.5-12.5)
acquisition of a kingdom or very high office (BPHS 47.56, 47.60)
a vipareeta-type rajayoga when a yogakaraka Saturn sits in a dusthana (Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, example of K. Karunakaran)
travel to Western or foreign countries (Raman p. 260, Saturn in Libra or Aquarius)

by_area.personality: Laziness, wrongdoing and bad company in the general texts (Phaladeepika 19.13); when well disposed, intelligence, enthusiasm and many undertakings (Uttara Kalamrita sec. 6, sl. 11.5-12.5). Raman's sign results range from philosophical study and mental peace (Sagittarius) to distrust and unrest (Leo).
by_area.career: Recognition from government, command or high office, success in learning when Saturn is strong or in the 3rd/11th (BPHS 47.53-56); headship of a village, trade or a guild (Jataka Parijata 18.121; Uttara Kalamrita); loss of position and government displeasure when in a dusthana, debilitated or combust (BPHS 47.57-58).
by_area.finance: Gain of wealth, land and property when well placed (BPHS 47.53-56; Uttara Kalamrita); farming losses and sudden loss of land and wealth in the general description (Phaladeepika 19.13); loss of wealth when Saturn is malefic (Uttara Kalamrita).
by_area.health: Wind ailments such as gout or rheumatism, phlegm disorders, piles, burning in the limbs (Phaladeepika 19.13, 19.23); injury from poison or weapons when Saturn is in a dusthana, debilitated or combust (BPHS 47.57); disease and becoming crippled when Saturn is malefic (Uttara Kalamrita).
by_area.relationships: Trouble and illness for spouse and children (Phaladeepika 19.13, 19.23; BPHS 47.58); happiness from spouse and birth of children when well placed (BPHS 47.56).
by_area.family: Separation from father, and in the Sanskrit gloss from mother too (BPHS 47.58); misunderstandings among relatives in some signs (Raman p. 259); sudden loss of relatives (Phaladeepika 19.13).
by_area.spirituality: Performance of sacrifices and rituals when Saturn is well disposed (Uttara Kalamrita sec. 6, sl. 11.5-12.5); pilgrimage and religious study with Saturn in Sagittarius or Pisces (Raman p. 260).

strengtheners: Saturn exalted, in its own, moolatrikona or a friend's sign, or in its own or exalted navamsa (BPHS 47.53)
Saturn in a kendra or trikona, in Sagittarius or Pisces, with or aspected by benefics, or joined with a yogakaraka (BPHS 47.59)
Saturn as yogakaraka for Taurus and Libra lagnas (BPHS 34.23-24, 34.33-34; Santhanam's note to BPHS 47.60)
Saturn exalted in the navamsa while debilitated in the rasi: the dasa ends well (Jataka Parijata 18.132)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saturn in the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated or combust (BPHS 47.57)
as a malefic, in debilitation, an enemy sign, the 6th or the 12th: severe suffering (Phaladeepika 20.27)
Saturn's dasa as the fourth dasa of life (Phaladeepika 20.24; Raman p. 230)
Saturn exalted in the rasi but debilitated in the navamsa: the dasa ends badly (Jataka Parijata 18.132)
planets in the 6th from Saturn turn hostile through the dasa (Rath, Crux p. 330, citing Sarvartha Chintamani)
lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS ch. 34 (tr. Santhanam vol. 1) gives Saturn's functional role by lagna. It is auspicious and gives rajayoga for Taurus (34.23-24) and is auspicious for Libra (34.33-34) and Aquarius (34.41-42). It is a malefic or killer for Aries, mainly when related to Venus (34.19-22), and for Cancer (34.27-28), Leo (34.29-30), Scorpio (34.35-36), Sagittarius (34.37-38) and Pisces (34.43-44). For Capricorn it does not kill on its own (34.39-40). Phaladeepika 20.60 judges a dasa lord's effect at any time by the house it is transiting from the Moon. Rath (Crux p. 330) treats Saturn's sign as a temporary lagna during the dasa: malefics in houses Saturn signifies (e.g. the 8th from it) spoil those matters, and benefics there improve them. PVR Narasimha Rao uses the Sun as the main reference point for judging a mahadasha.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.52-60, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 584-585
source_views.view: Calls Saturn the lowest of the planets. Exalted, in own, moolatrikona or friendly sign, in own or exalted navamsa, and in the 3rd or 11th: recognition from government, opulence, fame, success in education, conveyances, wealth, command of an army, a kingdom, Lakshmi's favour, property and children. In the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated or combust: poison, weapon injuries, separation from father, distress to wife and children, disaster from government displeasure, imprisonment. With or aspected by a benefic, in a kendra or trikona, in Sagittarius or Pisces: kingdom or high office, conveyances and clothes. Translator's note: as kendra-trikona lord Saturn is yogakaraka for Taurus and Libra lagnas and does very well if unafflicted.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.52-60, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: Verse 53 also lists the 9th house among the good positions; verse 54 ties royal honour, fame, wealth and scholarly debate to the 3rd and 11th; verse 57 adds loss of position and great fear; verse 58 adds separation from mother; verse 59 adds union with a yogakaraka and the 11th (labha) house to the good conditions.

Saturn's functional role by lagna: rajayoga-giver for Taurus; auspicious for Libra and Aquarius; malefic or killer for Aries (if related to Venus), Cancer, Leo, Scorpio, Sagittarius and Pisces; not a killer on its own for Capricorn.

19.13: wind ailments such as gout in wife and children, farming losses, gossip, bad company, servants leaving, long absence from home, sudden loss of relatives, land, comfort and wealth. 19.23: gains of servants, elderly women and cattle through national unrest; trouble to children and wife; wind and phlegm disorders, piles, burning in the limbs.

20.24: Saturn's dasa falling fourth in the sequence is dangerous. 20.27: malefics in debilitation, an enemy sign, the 6th or 12th cause severe suffering in their dasas. 20.31: among Saturn, Mandi, Rahu, the 22nd-drekkana lord and the 8th lord, only the weakest gives a fatal dasa, with death when Saturn transits the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna. 20.57: a combust, debilitated or enemy-sign planet in an auspicious sign or navamsa gives a mixed dasa that improves in its second half.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.121 and 18.132 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri vol. 2)
source_views.view: 18.121: goats, asses, camels, old women, birds and coarse grain; wealth from running a guild, trade body or village community; may rule a low tribe. 18.132: Saturn in its debilitation navamsa while in its exaltation sign gives happiness at the start and misery at the end; in its exaltation navamsa while in its debilitation sign, trouble from robbers and enemies, misery and roaming abroad at the start, happiness at the end.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita Kanda I sec. 6, sl. 11.5-12.5 (English edition on archive.org; P.S. Sastri's translation, ch. VI, agrees)
source_views.view: A well-disposed Saturn gives prosperity, intelligence, sacrifices and rituals, lands, headship of a village or town, success as a merchant and in many activities. A malefic Saturn gives poisoning, loss of wealth, bodily trouble, the ruler's anger, forbidden acts, being crippled and disease.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, pp. 230-232 and 259-260
source_views.view: General rule: Saturn's dasa as the 4th dasa is unfavourable. By sign: Aries the worst period, with losses, failures and more enemies; Taurus agricultural gains and much income; Gemini recognition, profits in trade and speculation, political success; Cancer miseries, family strife, illness; Leo unease, distrust, misappropriation of money and prosecution if badly afflicted, hated by all and longing for death as relief; Virgo high position and business success; Libra foreign travel, new business branches, honour and domestic happiness; Scorpio odium of superiors, loss of prestige and property; Sagittarius philosophical study, marriages at home, peace; Capricorn more land, wealth and great friends; Aquarius travel in Western countries, success in litigation, wealth; Pisces pilgrimage and indifference to sectarian rules, but also sorrow and unrest.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events (1998), pp. 330-331 and the Karunakaran example
source_views.view: In Saturn's dasa, planets in the 6th from Saturn are very hostile throughout and show their harm in their own sub-periods (citing Sarvartha Chintamani). Houses Saturn signifies, counted from it, should hold benefics: e.g. Mars 8th from Saturn spoils spouse's health and debts in Saturn's dasa. Example: for a Taurus lagna, yogakaraka Saturn in the 3rd (a dusthana) gave a strong rajayoga through its dasa.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, ch. on planetary periods, pp. 199-204
source_views.view: The major lord gives the results of the houses it rules and aspects. A functionally benefic Saturn can still bring out its natural malefic nature when the other period lords are difficult. Advises remedial balancing at the start of a period, propitiating a malefic lord through mantra, ritual or worship.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, sec. 16.5-16.6
source_views.view: General method only, no Saturn-specific list: a planet gives in its dasa what its divisional-chart positions promise, and the Sun is the key reference point for a mahadasha. Ayur-dasa example: Saturn as 7th lord and Maheswara was a strong maraka, and J.F. Kennedy Jr. died in Saturn-Mercury.

disagreements: Phaladeepika 19.13 and Jataka Parijata 18.121 give mostly mixed or low-grade results without conditions, while BPHS and Uttara Kalamrita make the period strongly conditional and potentially excellent. Santhanam reads BPHS 47.53-56 as dignity together with the 3rd/11th placement. The Sanskrit gloss treats the dignities, the 9th house and the 3rd/11th as separate good conditions and adds the 11th to verse 59. Raman judges the dasa by Saturn's sign, rating Aries the worst and Libra or Capricorn favourable, which broadly follows dignity. He also rates Pisces mixed although BPHS lists Pisces as good. Phaladeepika 20.24 and Raman agree that Saturn's dasa is dangerous when it is the fourth dasa.
phrasing_guidance: Describe this as a long period of steady effort, responsibility and slow results, not as a disaster. Lead with the chart's actual conditions (dignity, house, functional role) and give the favourable version when they apply. Mention health in terms of joints, chronic or wind-type complaints and general care, never as a diagnosis. Do not predict death, imprisonment or the loss of a parent; at most suggest extra care for family elders and legal matters.

phases: Jataka Parijata 18.132 is the only text that gives phases specific to Saturn: exalted in the rasi but in its debilitation navamsa, the dasa starts happily and ends in misery; debilitated in the rasi but in its exaltation navamsa, it starts with trouble, enemies and wandering abroad and ends happily. Phaladeepika 20.57 gives a general rule: a combust, debilitated or enemy-sign planet in an auspicious sign or navamsa gives a mixed dasa that improves in its second half.
